**Where with_skill and without_skill diverged clearly:**
- In "cloudtrail-cost-severity-definitions", with_skill passed 100% of expected-output checks and all 18 assertions (high confidence), while without_skill failed 100% of the same checks (0/18 assertions, also high confidence) — a clean, high-confidence divergence favoring with_skill on this eval. with_skill's output was also fully consistent across runs, while without_skill's was only "mostly consistent."
- In "cloudtrail-cost-artifact-naming", the single filename-format assertion passed for with_skill (3/3) and failed for without_skill (0/3), another clean divergence favoring with_skill. without_skill's output consistency here was only "mostly consistent" (with_skill's consistency data wasn't available for this eval).

**Where both variants performed identically (assertion not discriminating):**
- "cloudtrail-cost-billing-model": both hit 100% on expected output and all 9 assertions (all "always_passes" pattern — this eval isn't distinguishing the variants on pass/fail). However, a quality-comparison layer here favored with_skill in 8 of 9 evaluated pairs (accuracy, actionability, completeness), with medium confidence, while with_skill also ran slightly longer (6s vs 5s) and cost slightly more ($0.05 vs $0.04) — a runtime/cost tradeoff against a quality edge. with_skill's output was fully consistent; without_skill's was "mostly consistent."
- "cloudtrail-cost-duplicate-reasoning": both variants passed 100% of expected output and all 12 assertions identically. Notably, the trigger itself did not fire in this eval (0/3), which is an important caveat — the underlying test condition may not have been exercised as intended. Consistency data was only available for without_skill (consistent); with_skill's consistency was not reported (null).
- "cloudtrail-cost-dedup-exclusion-interaction": both variants tied at 67% assertion pass rate (6/9), with the same assertion ("warns of coverage/audit gap") failing for both — indicating that specific behavior is not being met by either variant, a gap in the agent behavior (or possibly the assertion itself) rather than a difference between variants. Trigger also did not fire here (0/3), another caveat. Only without_skill had consistency data reported ("mostly consistent").

**Trigger-fired anomalies:** Three evals ("duplicate-reasoning", "dedup-exclusion-interaction", "artifact-naming") show trigger_fired at 0/3 despite expected-output and assertion checks still producing results — this suggests the trigger-detection measurement itself may be unreliable or not applicable in these cases, and should be treated as missing/uncertain data rather than a finding about either variant.

**Skipped eval:** "cloudtrail-cost-negative-trigger" was a should-not-trigger test; trigger_fired passed 3/3 (correctly not triggering), and all other dimensions were intentionally skipped as not applicable.

**Quality comparisons:** Only one eval (billing-model) had quality pairs actually evaluated (3 pairs, medium confidence, favoring with_skill on most criteria); the other four chat evals with quality sections all had pairs_skipped=3/pairs_evaluated=0, meaning no comparative quality judgment could be made there.

**Overall:** with_skill showed clean, high-confidence advantages on two evals (severity-definitions, artifact-naming) and a quality edge with a small time/cost cost on billing-model; the two variants were statistically tied (identical pass/fail patterns) on duplicate-reasoning and dedup-exclusion-interaction, the latter also revealing a shared behavioral gap (audit-gap warning) neither variant satisfies. Several consistency and trigger-fired fields are missing or only available for one variant, and some quality comparisons couldn't be computed at all, limiting how much can be concluded from those specific dimensions.
